name: Helez
overview: Helez was a male warrior known as the Paltite (or Pelonite in 1 Chronicles 11:27) and was counted as the tenth member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not specified in the biblical record. Beyond his role among David's warriors, Scripture provides no further personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Helez means "vigor" or "he has saved," reflecting a sense of strength or deliverance. This proper name is noted in 2 Samuel 23:26 but was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Helez beyond what is indicated in his designation as the Paltite (Pelonite). There are no listed relatives or familial connections in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Helez's significance lies in his role as one of David's mighty men, specifically as the tenth of "the thirty," a distinguished band of warriors who supported King David. His inclusion among these elite fighters highlights his valor and importance in David's military campaigns. Though details are sparse, his mention underscores the strength and loyalty that contributed to David's reign.
